title: The Top of Mount Everest Is Made of Seashells

scenes.text: The top of Mount Everest is made of seashells.
The summit rock is limestone, packed with the shells of ancient sea creatures.
470 million years ago, that rock was the floor of a warm, shallow sea.
Then India crashed into Asia and shoved the sea floor five and a half miles into the sky.
The crash is still going. Everest grows a few millimetres every year.
So every climber up there is standing on an ancient ocean floor. Seashells, on the roof of the world.

description:
The top of Mount Everest is made of seashells.
The summit limestone formed on the floor of a warm sea about 470 million years ago, then India crashed into Asia and pushed it 8,849 metres into the sky. The collision continues, so Everest is still growing.
What other mountain do you think used to be underwater?
first_comment: Bonus: the summit rock is so cooked by heat and pressure that geologists call it a low-grade metamorphic rock. Which mountain should we check next?
